texts.facts: 1 . In this case, a Detailed Accident Report was filed by police in terms of provisions of Motor Vehicle Act qua injuries sustained by Ms. Manisha Gupta W/o Late Sh. Sunil Gupta in an accident on 16.01.2020 caused due to rash and negligent driving of Wagon R car bearing Registration No. DL1R TB 7748 (hereinafter referred as the offending vehicle) being driven by Sh. Pawan Kumar (hereinafter referred as the respondent no.1), owned by Sh. Hemant Sharma (hereinafter referred as the owner) which has been treated as Claim Petition in view of the provisions contained in such Act. Preliminary information regarding accident in question was received at PS Hazrat Nizamuddin vide PCR Call registered as DD No. 11A and 12A upon receipt of which HC Satender alongwith Ct. Jagbir went to the spot of accident at Pant Nagar Bus Stand, Lala Lajpat Rai Marg, Jangpura Extension, Delhi, where a white colour Wagon R bearing Registration No. DL1R TB 7748 was found in accidental condition alongwith its driver, who revealed his name as Pawan Kumar and informed that the injured woman has been shifted to hospital by PCR. Ct. Jagbir was left at the spot while HC Satender left for AIIMS Trauma Center, where MLC of injured Manisha Gupta was collected and she was interrogated. A written complaint was subsequently filed on 19.01.2020 by injured Manisha Gupta, wherein she narrated that she had hired one Ola Cab (White colour Wagon R) with Registration No. DL1R TB 7748 driven by Pawan Kumar, on 16.01.2020 at 7.55 AM from Press Enclave Marg to MACT No 353/2021 Manisha Guupta vs. Pawan Kumar & Ors. Page No. 2 of 3 reach NABET, CGO Complex. She mentioned that the Cab crashed into the divider when it was crossing Defence Colony Flyover near Pant Nagar Bus Stand due to irresponsible and negligent driving of the Cab driver. She also mentioned that she was not in a state to give her statement on 16.01.2020. FIR was registered. Investigation was carried out. Offending vehicle was seized and mechanical inspection was got conducted. MLC of injured was collected wherein injuries were opined to be grievous. Notice under Section 133 of M.V. Act was served upon registered owner, who stated that the offending vehicle was sold to Pawan Kumar much before date of accident therefore Pawan Kumar was driver as well as owner/possession holder on the date of accident. During investigation it was revealed that the offending vehilce was without a valid and effective insurance and as such, penal provisions of MV Act were added. Upon completion of investigation, charge- sheet was filed under Sections 279/338 IPC and under Section 146/196 of MV Act, against driver Pawan Kumar and owner Hemant Sharma. DAR was filed by Investigating Officer before this Tribunal on 06.04.2021. 3. Show cause notice was issued to the driver as well as owner as to why they should not be directed to furnish sufficient security deposit at least to the tune of Rs.90,000/- alongwith the affidavit of their income and assets vide order dated 03.04.2021 but any response to the same was not received. 4. On the first date of hearing, driver did not appear despite Pabandinama served by the Investigating Officer. Subsequently, notice was issued to Pawan Kumar by Court, which was served upon him to appear on 15.01.2022 but he chose not to appear in the Court. No reply to DAR or show cause notice was filed by him. MACT No 353/2021 Manisha Guupta vs. Pawan Kumar & Ors. Page No. 3 of 3 5. Reply to DAR was filed on behalf of R-2. It was stated by counsel for R-2 that the same be treated as reply to the show cause notice as well. In the said reply, it is stated that the alleged offending vehicle was sold to respondent no.1 on 21.06.2019 and even Form 29 and 30 were executed. He has also filed copy of bank statement to prove the transaction as annexed with the reply. It is also stated that the vehicle was in complete physical and legal possession with respondent no.1 and it was for respondent no.1 to explain as to why he did not get the Registration Certificate transferred in his name. It is also stated that the vehicle was duly insured at the time of handing over its possession. Manisha Gupta (Dar) vs Pawan Kumar on 27 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141743782/ 2 6. Directions were given vide order dated 17.03.2023 for cancellation of Superdari and for auction of the offending vehicle. As the security deposit is not furnished, right to contest the petition on behalf of respondents was closed, however they were granted right to cross-examine the claimant's witnesses. 7. An application seeking assessment of physical disability of injured/claimant by Medical Board was moved and allowed vide order dated 31.03.2023, which was allowed. As per Disability Assessment Report, 16% permanent physical impairment in relation to spine has been opined by Medical Board. OPP. 3) Relief. 9. Matter was then listed for Petitioner Evidence. Petitioner appeared as PW-1 and tendered her evidentiary affidavit as Ex.PW1/1. She relied upon MLC of injured Ex.PW1/A, Discharge Summary of injured issued by AIIMS Trauma Center Ex.PW1/B, Discharge Summary of injured issued by Ram Lal Kundan Lal Hospital Ex.PW1/C, DAR Ex.PW1/D, Salary slip of injured Mark-A, Medical Bills Ex.PW1/E, Conveyance Ticket Ex.PW1/F, Copy of Adhar Card of injured Ex.PW1/G, Copy of PAN of injured Ex.PW1/H. 10. Cross-examination was deferred as none appeared on behalf of any of the respondents for cross-examination of PW1, however still none appeared on behalf of respondents therefore, opportunity to cross-examine PW1 was closed. 11. As none appeared on behalf of respondents and also as their right to contest was closed vide order dated 17.03.2023, Respondents Evidence was also closed vide order dated 27.02.2024. 12. Final arguments advanced by counsel for claimant, who stated that compensation may be decided as per law. 13. None appeared on behalf of respondents to advance arguments. 16. Police after investigation had filed charge-sheet against respondent no.1 under Section 279/338 IPC which is also suggestive of negligence of respondent no.1 in causing the accident.

Mahadeva Shetty & Anr., reported as (2003) 7 SCC 197, needs mention here (para 15): "Statutory provisions clearly indicate that the compensation must be "just" and it cannot be a bonanza; not a source of profit but the same should not be a pittance. The courts and tribunals have a duty to weigh the various factors and quantify the amount of compensation, which should be just. What would be "just" compensation is a vexed question. There can be no golden rule applicable to all cases for measuring the value of human life or a limb. Measure of damages cannot be arrived at by precise mathematical calculations. It would depend upon the particular facts and circumstances, and attending peculiar or special features, if any. Every method or mode adopted for assessing compensation has to be considered in the background of "just" compensation which is the pivotal consideration. Though by use of the expression "which appears to it to be just", a wide discretion is vested in the Tribunal, the determination has to be rational, to be done by a judicious approach and not the outcome of whims, wild guesses and arbitrariness.. ..." 25.
